sources.bodyExcerpt: Guitar Pedal X - GPX Blog - 9 of the Best MI Audio / MI Effects Pedals ao link News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Xploration • Curation • Recommendation News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index News GPX AI Forums Notifications Popular Highlights 4 of a Kind 12 Degrees of Saturation ArtistArray Best in Class Best of Brands Builder Profiles Colours Expo Guitar Pedal 101 Iconic Gear In Memoriam Pedal Chain Pedal Planet Trifecta Versus Index Enter a search term Search Remember Login Register | Reset Password Filter content by area of interest Amps Boost and Overdrive Delay Distortion Fuzz Guitars Modulation Pitch Reverb Utility All All 9 of the Best MI Audio / MI Effects Pedals Oct 28, 2018 00:58 by Stefan Karlsson Best of Brands Boost Boost and Overdrive Brown Sound Distortion Delay Digital Delay Distortion Effects Pedal Makers Fuzz Germanium Fuzz Klone and Transparent Overdrive Lo-Fi Delay Metal Distortion MI Audio MI Effects Michael Ibrahim Octave Fuzz Overdrive Silicon Fuzz Tubescreamer Style Overdrive + - Full Article Read Summary Key Points MI Effects makes compact V1 and larger V2 overdrive, fuzz, delay and high‑gain pedals with multi‑control “tweaker” topologies. Distribution is limited in the UK; buys have been via Reverb, Haar Guitars (Netherlands) and Musik Produktiv (Germany). Blue Boy Deluxe Overdrive V1 — Tube‑Screamer style, Bright/Mids/Tone/Character. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £100. Cross Over Drive V2 — 4 FET stages, 2‑band EQ. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £120. GI Fuzz V1 — Bias/Load/Bright toggle. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £120. Lo‑Fi Delay — PT2399, 600ms. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £120. Megalith Delta V2 — high gain, Contour/EQ Shift. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £230. Neo Fuzz V1 — AC128 germanium. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £120. Pollyanna Octave Synth Fuzz V1 — two down/one up octaves. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £120. Super Blues Pro — TS‑style core, silicon/MOSFET clipping. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £120. Super Crunch Box V2 — brown‑sound, 3‑band EQ+Presence. As of 2026-07-13, the price was £121. Megalith Delta and Super Crunch Box are described as permanent pedal‑chain fixtures; Lo‑Fi Delay, Pollyanna and Super Blues Pro remain to be acquired. Readers of this blog will know that I’m quite the fan of Michael Ibrahim’s MI Effects Pedals. I’ve had two as a permanent fixture in my pedal-chain for quite a considerable time already - the Super Crunch Box V2 and the super high gain Megalith Delta - which are both exceptional performers in their respective categories. I’ve long had a number of his other pedals in my sight too - in particular his two earlier V1 compact fuzzes - the G.I. and Neo - or Silicon and Germanium versions. I was much encouraged by the recent Andy Martin ’That Pedal Show’ episode to finally snap up one each of these - used, but in very good condition - the compact Neo would seem to be one of Andy’s favourite fuzzes. Of the newer pedals, the only one not included here is the V5 Boost ’N’ Buff - for which I think there are cleverer equivalents available - like the Jackson Audio Prism and ThorpyFX Team Medic for example. The Cross Over Drive, Lo-Fi Delay and Super Blues Pro are all really smart pedals - with their multip
